bias.label: Leaning down below 3,590; fresh low near 3,516

event: US Michigan consumer sentiment (final, Nov) and Fed remarks, Fri 20 Nov 17:00 SAST (time UNVERIFIED).

bullets.title: Another sharp drop
bullets.text: Gold fell about 3-4% more overnight and traded near 3,531 at 06:37 SAST, after a low of 3,516.50 on Kitco around 06:14 SAST.

bullets.title: Fed hike priced
bullets.text: Mitrade says markets price roughly a 90% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike on 8-9 December, and several big banks now forecast hikes.

bullets.title: Dollar and yields
bullets.text: The dollar is near a 19-month high and the US 10-year yield is about 5.05%, both heavy weights on gold.

bullets.title: Broad risk selloff
bullets.text: Stocks fell hard too (S&P 500 down about 2%, Asian markets red), so gold is being sold alongside everything else.

bullets.title: Oil shock backdrop
bullets.text: Hormuz shipping disruption keeps Brent near 92 dollars, which feeds inflation and hike fears rather than safe-haven buying.

bullets.title: Quotes disagree
bullets.text: Sources show prices from 3,516 to 3,579 this morning, so check your own chart before using any level here.

levels.note: Mitrade's support zone, now broken; first area a bounce must clear

watch: Catching a falling knife. Gold has dropped over 200 dollars in two days; wait for the hold.
A 1H close under 3,490 opens the 3,450-3,475 zone. Step aside.
The Michigan data and Fed speakers at 17:00 SAST can whip price both ways.
Moving your stop lower when price gets close. That is how a small loss becomes a big one.
